LESSON: ROUNDERS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.6: Rounders

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rounders. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do fielding skills help players in a Rounders game?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation
2. identify materials and tools used in carving
3. value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ROUNDERS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rounders helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ROUNDERS
Study Rounders like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rounders” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify materials and tools used in carving

What this means
In this part you learn to identify materials and tools used in carving. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify materials and tools used in carving.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rounders in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify materials and tools used in carving. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders

What this means
In this part you learn to value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rounders is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rounders” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rounders in your own words. (skill: identify materials and tools used in carving)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rounders to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation.
3. Practise this skill: identify materials and tools used in carving.
4. Practise this skill: value the safety of self and others when playing the game of Rounders.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rounders from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rounders: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Rounders?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do fielding skills help players in a Rounders game?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rounders means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the features of a rounders bat for familiarisation.
5. Be able to: identify materials and tools used in carving.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
